Welcome to Barham
A happy, thriving school
Our vision is for every child to be kind, confident and curious
A rich curriculum: music, sport, arts and outdoor learning
OPAL, beautiful grounds and our swimming pool
Welcome to Barham Church of England Primary School
It is a privilege to be the Headteacher of our friendly village school, situated in the beautiful Kent Downs near Canterbury. We are proud of our strong Christian ethos, our close links with St John’s Church and our place at the heart of the local community.
At Barham, we know, nurture and value every child. Our values of being kind, confident and curious are at the heart of school life. We provide a warm and supportive environment where children feel safe, happy and encouraged to become enthusiastic, independent learners.
Our broad and creative curriculum enables children to explore their interests, develop their unique gifts and talents, and achieve their personal best. Alongside academic learning, children enjoy a wide range of opportunities through music, sport, art, drama, dance, outdoor learning and play. We are also fortunate to have extensive grounds, Outdoor Play and Learning (OPAL), Forest School and our own swimming pool.
Choosing the right school for your child is an important decision. We warmly invite you to visit us, meet our staff and children, and experience our wonderful school community for yourself.
If you would like further information or would like to arrange a visit, please contact the school office on 01227 831312. We would be delighted to welcome you.

Kingfisher Breakfast & After School Club
Kingfisher Breakfast and After School Club
Welcome to Kingfisher Breakfast and After School Club. Our club provides a safe, caring and engaging environment for children before and after the school day.
Kingfisher Club phone number for calls and texts: 07508841215. This number will only be monitored during the hours of the Club.
Kingfisher email address: kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk. This inbox will be monitored during the school day.
At Kingfisher Club we encourage children to be Kind, Confident and Curious.
At Kingfisher Club our rules are to be: Ready, Respectful and Safe.
Breakfast Club: 7:45am–8:35am
Early Session: 3:15pm–4:30pm
Late Session: 3:15pm–6:00pm
On days when the school finishes at 2:15pm (which is usually the last day of the Christmas and Summer terms), session times will be adjusted by an hour. The Early Session will run from 2:15pm to 3:30pm and the Late Session will run from 2:15pm to 5:00pm.
The club is based in the art room. Children will benefit from using the whole school site.
The Club Manager is Mrs Kim Ward. Kim is a Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL). All Kingfisher staff will follow the school’s safeguarding, behaviour and welfare procedures.
Arrival and Collection: Breakfast Club
Parents drop their child off at the Breakfast Club via the side gate. When arriving to drop off, parents need to press the "3" button on the side gate intercom. A member of staff will come and meet your child from the gate. Children will be signed in by a member of staff. A member of staff will escort the children to their respective classes at 8:35 a.m. If your child is booked onto a breakfast session and they can no longer attend, please contact the club.
Arrival and Collection: After School Club
At 3.15pm KS1 children will be collected from their classes and taken to the club and KS2 children will go independently.
When arriving to collect, parents need to press the "3" button on the side gate intercom for Kingfishers. A member of staff will bring your child to meet you at the gate. Please inform the club if somebody different will be collecting your child. If your child is booked onto an after-school session and they can no longer attend, please contact the club.
Safeguarding and Behaviour
The club follows all existing school policies relating to safeguarding, behaviour, attendance, medical needs and online safety. These policies are available on our school website. Any disciplinary issues will be reported to parents. Repeated breaches of the behaviour policy may result in the child being removed from the club. Policies can be found here: https://barham.kent.sch.uk/information/policies
A healthy breakfast will be provided. Fruit will be readily available at all sessions.
For the Early After School Club sessions, children can bring a snack that must be nut-free.
For the Late After School Club sessions, children are welcome to bring a couple of snacks or a packed lunch. In accordance with current school rules, packed lunches should not contain fizzy drinks, canned drinks, sweets, nuts or nut-based products including chocolate spread.
Please ensure the school is informed about allergies or dietary requirements.
Children will have access to a range of activities including crafts, games, reading, outdoor play and quiet relaxation areas. In accordance with current school rules, children are not permitted to bring in their own toys from home.
Please ensure that all medical information and emergency contact details are kept up to date. Medication procedures follow the school policy. If a child requires first aid treatment, this will be recorded on Medical Tracker and parents will receive a notification via email. As per the school policy, if a child hurts their head a phone call home will be made.
Breakfast Club (7:45am–8:35am): £4.00 per session
Early Session (3:15pm–4:30pm): £5.00 per session
Late Session (3:15pm–6:00pm): £10.00 per session
Children in receipt of Targeted Pupil Premium can attend Breakfast Club and the Early session free of charge, subject to places being available. There will be a charge for the late session.
Parents must complete a registration form before a booking can be made.
Parents are required to book their sessions via Arbor. Payment is taken at the time of booking. Click here for Arbor's guide on booking a Breakfast or After School Club via the Parent Portal or Parent App.
If you wish to use Tax Free Childcare Vouchers towards payment, the school needs to have an account with the voucher provider. We already have accounts with: the Government’s Tax Free Childcare scheme (Provider reference 118653), Edenred (Account Number: P21361608) and Bravo Benefits. If you have a different voucher provider, please send the details to the Kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk, so an account can be created.
Once the school has an account with your voucher provider, you can send payments via their website/portal. Please e-mail Kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk to confirm the amount sent. Once the payment is received into the school’s bank account (which can take a few days), Arbor will be credited with the voucher amount, allowing you to book your sessions.
If your child has additional needs, please contact the club before booking.
On the day bookings will be accepted if there are spaces.
For enquiries or changes, please contact:
kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk or call or text 07508841215
Parents need to email kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk if they wish to cancel a session, or your child is unable to attend. No charge will be made where at least 24 hours’ notice is provided. Sessions cancelled with less than 24 hours’ notice will still be charged, except at the school’s discretion.
Please collect children promptly at the end of their booked session. If you are running late, please contact the club immediately. There is a fee of £15 per child for a late collection, and you will be sent an invoice.
Guidance and Standards
The club operates in line with Department of Education wraparound childcare guidance and NSPCC safeguarding guidance.
By using Kingfisher Club, parents and carers agree to follow school policies and procedures and work in partnership with staff to support a positive and safe environment.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Barham Church of England Primary School.
It is a privilege to be the Headteacher of our friendly village school, situated in the beautiful Kent Downs near Canterbury. We are proud of our strong Christian ethos, our close links with St John’s Church and our place at the heart of the local community.
At Barham, we know, nurture and value every child. Our values of being kind, confident and curious are at the heart of school life. We provide a warm and supportive environment where children feel safe, happy and encouraged to become enthusiastic, independent learners.
Our broad and creative curriculum enables children to explore their interests, develop their unique gifts and talents, and achieve their personal best. Alongside academic learning, children enjoy a wide range of opportunities through music, sport, art, drama, dance, outdoor learning and play. We are also fortunate to have extensive grounds, a Forest School and our own swimming pool.
Choosing the right school for your child is an important decision. We warmly invite you to visit us, meet our staff and children, and experience our wonderful school community for yourself.
If you would like further information or would like to arrange a visit, please contact the school office on 01227 831312. We would be delighted to welcome you.

School Dinners and Packed Lunches
Caterlink provide school dinners at Barham.
The cost of the meals for this academic year (2025-2026) is £3.37per meal. All meals for Key Stage 1 continue to be funded by the government.
Caterlink meals should be ordered via ParentPay and should done in advance – daily, weekly, monthly or termly. A "how to" guide on ordering can be found at: https://parentpay.wistia.com/medias/cd0pwrbiiv

Healthy Packed Lunches
The School Council met to discuss how important it is to eat healthily and to give parents and children some ideas of what to put in lunch boxes. Please click on the links below for some healthy options for packed lunches.
School council have agreed that the following are not allowed in packed lunches:
• Fizzy drinks or any drinks in glass bottles
• Nuts or nut-based products including chocolate spread that contains nuts (because of children with nut allergies)
Biscuits, cakes and crisps should be a rare treat only. School council agreed that any chocolate biscuits must contain more biscuit than chocolate. To ensure parents know exactly what their children have eaten, children will bring home any uneaten food in their packed lunch box.

Reading at Barham
At Barham Church of England Primary School, we believe that reading opens doors. It enables children to succeed across the curriculum, discover new ideas, understand different experiences and develop a lifelong love of learning.
At Barham Church of England Primary School, we believe that reading opens doors. It enables children to succeed across the curriculum, discover new ideas, understand different experiences and develop a lifelong love of learning.
Reading also helps our children grow to be kind, confident and curious. Books encourage kindness by helping children see the world through other people’s eyes; increasing fluency gives them confidence as readers and learners; and encountering new stories, information and ideas inspires curiosity.
Our aims for every reader
We want every child to:
* use secure phonics knowledge to decode unfamiliar words;
* read accurately, fluently and with expression;
* develop a rich and increasingly ambitious vocabulary;
* understand, discuss and respond thoughtfully to texts;
* retrieve information, make connections and explain ideas using evidence;
* experience a broad range of fiction, non-fiction and poetry;
* discover authors, genres and subjects that capture their interest; and
* choose to read for pleasure as well as for learning.
How reading is taught at Barham
Reading is taught through whole-class teaching, small-group work and individual practice. Children are taught the knowledge and skills they need to become successful readers, including decoding, fluency, vocabulary, retrieval, inference, prediction, summarising and evaluating an author’s choices.
High-quality books are used throughout our curriculum. These texts enrich children’s vocabulary and knowledge while providing exciting starting points for discussion, writing and learning in other subjects.
Teachers assess children’s reading regularly so that additional teaching and support can be provided promptly whenever it is needed.
Early reading and phonics
In Reception and Year 1, children receive a daily phonics lesson using Essential Letters and Sounds, a systematic synthetic phonics programme validated by the Department for Education.
Children learn the sounds represented by letters and groups of letters and how to blend these sounds to read words. They take home carefully selected decodable books containing the sounds they have already been taught. This allows them to practise successfully and develop accuracy, fluency and confidence.
Rereading the same decodable book is important. Each reading should become smoother and more expressive as the child becomes increasingly familiar with the words and meaning.
Phonics teaching continues in Year 2 and beyond for any child who needs further support. Teaching and intervention are carefully matched to each child’s needs so that they can make strong progress.
Developing fluency and understanding
As children become increasingly secure at decoding, teaching places greater emphasis on fluency, vocabulary and comprehension.
* read at an appropriate pace and with expression;
* discuss the meaning of unfamiliar words;
* identify important information;
* explain their ideas using evidence from the text;
* make sensible predictions and inferences;
* summarise what they have read; and
* compare texts, themes, characters and authors.
These skills are developed through carefully chosen fiction, non-fiction and poetry and are applied across the wider curriculum.
Reading for pleasure
Reading for pleasure is at the heart of school life. Our welcoming, well-stocked library provides children with access to an extensive selection of books, supported by our school librarian. Class book corners offer further opportunities for children to browse, explore and choose books that appeal to them.
Our reading spines include high-quality, engaging and inclusive texts. We want children to encounter familiar experiences while also discovering different cultures, perspectives, places and ways of life.
Choice is important. Novels, picture books, poetry, factual books, comics and graphic novels can all help children find their identity as readers.
Our reading spines and text maps
Our year-group text maps show the rich range of books children encounter during their time at Barham. They include texts used for reading instruction and writing, reading-for-pleasure choices, poetry and books linked to wider curriculum learning.
Supporting reading at home
Families make an invaluable contribution to children’s reading development. Regular reading at home gives children the individual encouragement, conversation and practice that help them flourish.
A few minutes of relaxed, positive reading regularly is often more beneficial than one long session. You can help by:
* finding a quiet and comfortable place to read;
* encouraging early readers to say the sounds and blend them together;
* rereading decodable books to build fluency and expression;
* reading aloud to your child, whatever their age;
* taking turns to read pages or sections;
* talking about new or interesting vocabulary;
* asking your child what they think rather than testing them on every page;
* encouraging a wide range of reading, including stories, poetry, information books, comics and magazines;
* visiting the local library and allowing your child to choose; and
* showing that you value reading by letting your child see you read.
Audiobooks can also be a wonderful way to experience stories and ambitious language. They can be enjoyed alongside, rather than instead of, opportunities to practise independent reading.
Our Reading Together at Home leaflet contains further guidance.
If your child finds reading difficult or you are unsure how best to support them, please speak to their class teacher. We will be pleased to work with you and suggest strategies or books appropriate to their stage of reading.
Finding your child’s next book
The following websites offer useful, current recommendations:
* BookTrust Bookfinder – recommendations by age and interest
* LoveReading4Kids – reviews, recommendations and age-guided book lists
* Centre for Literacy in Primary Education – high-quality primary booklists
* UKLA Book Awards – outstanding children’s books chosen by teachers
* The Carnegies – award-winning writing and illustration
* The Reading Agency – including the annual Summer Reading Challenge

School History
Barham Primary School was originally founded in 1858 in the Parish of St John the Baptist to give village children a sound education within a Christian framework. Since that time the popularity of the school has resulted in children being welcomed from a much wider area. Barham is a Church of England Voluntary Controlled Primary School for children aged 4 to 11. Our official capacity is 210 pupils and our admission limit in any one year is 30 children.
The school is situated at the heart of the village in Valley Road, opposite the green.
The school has grown considerably since it was built in 1858. The original Victorian building houses the administration offices, the Headteacher’s office and two classrooms. Over the years mobile classrooms were added to meet the growing demand for places at the school. In 2000 a whole suite of new buildings was added to the school. Further extensive works were carried out to enlarge and modernise the old building whilst maintaining its character. Building works and renovations were completed in 2002. We now have seven excellent classrooms, including a purpose-built foundation stage classroom, a large multi-purpose hall and studio. We are also fortunate in having dedicated rooms for art and music, plus a swimming pool.
We have a good, flat playground, some small garden areas and a large playing field. We also have a quiet area for moments of reflection In addition, from some parts of the site, there are some outstanding views of the village and the valley in which it resides.
Organisation
Our organisation is typical of a school of this size, having one class per year group. This is very advantageous for teachers in terms of planning and delivering the curriculum. Our admission limit means that the school is unlikely to grow any larger, so in many ways we have the perfect compromise, the feel and atmosphere of a small school, without the challenges of mixed aged classes.

Music at Barham
Every child a musician
Music is at the heart of life at Barham. We want every child to experience the joy of making music and to see themselves as a musician.
From Reception to Year 6, pupils receive regular music teaching led by specialist teachers. Children learn to listen, sing, compose, play and perform, developing their musical knowledge and skills as they progress through the school.
Our aim is to nurture a lifelong love of music while helping every child become kind, confident and curious.
Kind, confident and curious through music
Children learn to listen to one another, work as part of an ensemble and appreciate music from different cultures, traditions and periods. They encourage each other and celebrate one another’s achievements.
Children develop the confidence to express themselves, learn an instrument and perform for different audiences. Performance opportunities range from informal classroom sharing to concerts, competitions, church services and full-scale musical productions.
Children explore different instruments, composers, genres and musical traditions. They improvise, compose and investigate how music is created, including through the use of music technology.
Our music curriculum
Music is taught throughout the school and includes:
In Early Years, music is woven into children’s learning through singing, movement, listening and musical play. As pupils progress through the school, they develop increasing accuracy, fluency, control and expression.
Weekly music lessons
Regular whole-school singing
Singing, composing, improvising and performing
Opportunities to evaluate and improve performances
Music beyond the classroom
Our musical opportunities extend far beyond weekly lessons. Depending on the programme available each year, these include:
Individual and small-group instrumental tuition
Choir, band and instrumental clubs
Young Musician of the Year
Our annual inter-house music competition
Spring music performances
Talent shows and celebration assemblies
Key Stage 1 Nativity performances
Church services and community events
An annual Key Stage 2 musical production
Collaborative events with other schools and musicians
Children have performed at venues including the Gulbenkian Theatre, Canterbury Cathedral, Broome Park and St John’s Church. We also work with Kent Music, local secondary schools and visiting professional musicians to broaden pupils’ musical experiences.
“Music at Barham is fun!”
Learning an instrument
Children can access tuition in a range of instruments, which may include piano, drums, guitar, flute, brass, violin and other orchestral instruments.
For current information about available lessons, costs and teachers, please contact the school office:
Telephone: 01227 831312
Email: office@barham.kent.sch.uk
Our commitment
We believe that musical opportunity should be available to every child. Whole-class instruments are provided by the school, and teaching is adapted so that pupils with different needs and starting points can participate successfully.
Music brings our school community together. It gives children opportunities to discover new talents, experience the excitement of performing and create memories that last well beyond their time at Barham.

Sports Premium Funding
At Barham we believe that physical education provides a vital and unique contribution to a pupil’s physical and emotional development. For another year running, we have been awarded the GOLD Sports Mark Award! Our vision for PE and Sport is to provide high quality PE and Sport for all children in school. We aim to provide both competitive opportunities for extra-curricular sport and well planned and delivered PE lessons, which develop a love of sport for all children and an understanding of the importance of exercise in maintaining a healthy lifestyle.
We have a long tradition of sporting excellence and pupils have represented the country in dance, gymnastics and golf.
We are proud of the current PE curriculum provision at our school, which includes an annual dance festival and sports week - this is a whole week dedicated to giving children opportunities to take part in physical activity as well as introducing pupils to new sports such as Ultimate Frisbee and Triathlon
Barham has its own swimming pool which enables all our pupils from reception through to Year 6 to have regular swimming lessons. In addition to the two hours of PE a week, all classes take part in ten minutes of daily physical activity.
We provide all of our Year 6 pupils with a residential experience and the opportunity to participate in adventurous activities such as wall climbing, high ropes and dry-slope skiing.
Clubs over the last two years have included: Football, Girls football, Dodge ball, Fitness Fun, Splash Club (Swimming), Cross-country, , Basketball/netball, Gymnastics, Multi-skills, Outdoor games, Rugby, Dance, Cricket, Ultimate Frisbee and Rounders.
In addition, to the clubs mentioned above, we run a Young Leaders program for our Year 6 pupils who lead lunchtime activities in the summer term for our younger pupils.
Yoga and Forest School take place every year for different year groups so that every child will experience these sessions by the time they leave school.

The club is based in the art room. Children will benefit from using the whole school site.
The Club Manager is Mrs Kim Ward. Kim is a Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL). All Kingfisher staff will follow the school’s safeguarding, behaviour and welfare procedures.
Arrival and Collection: Breakfast Club
Parents drop their child off at the Breakfast Club via the side gate. When arriving to drop off, parents need to press the "3" button on the side gate intercom. A member of staff will come and meet your child from the gate. Children will be signed in by a member of staff. A member of staff will escort the children to their respective classes at 8:35 a.m. If your child is booked onto a breakfast session and they can no longer attend, please contact the club.
Arrival and Collection: After School Club
At 3.15pm KS1 children will be collected from their classes and taken to the club and KS2 children will go independently.
When arriving to collect, parents need to press the "3" button on the side gate intercom for Kingfishers. A member of staff will bring your child to meet you at the gate. Please inform the club if somebody different will be collecting your child. If your child is booked onto an after-school session and they can no longer attend, please contact the club.
Safeguarding and Behaviour
The club follows all existing school policies relating to safeguarding, behaviour, attendance, medical needs and online safety. These policies are available on our school website. Any disciplinary issues will be reported to parents. Repeated breaches of the behaviour policy may result in the child being removed from the club. Policies can be found here: https://barham.kent.sch.uk/information/policies
A healthy breakfast will be provided. Fruit will be readily available at all sessions.
For the Early After School Club sessions, children can bring a snack that must be nut-free.
For the Late After School Club sessions, children are welcome to bring a couple of snacks or a packed lunch. In accordance with current school rules, packed lunches should not contain fizzy drinks, canned drinks, sweets, nuts or nut-based products including chocolate spread.
Please ensure the school is informed about allergies or dietary requirements.
Children will have access to a range of activities including crafts, games, reading, outdoor play and quiet relaxation areas. In accordance with current school rules, children are not permitted to bring in their own toys from home.
Please ensure that all medical information and emergency contact details are kept up to date. Medication procedures follow the school policy. If a child requires first aid treatment, this will be recorded on Medical Tracker and parents will receive a notification via email. As per the school policy, if a child hurts their head a phone call home will be made.
Breakfast Club (7:45am–8:35am): £4.00 per session
Early Session (3:15pm–4:30pm): £5.00 per session
Late Session (3:15pm–6:00pm): £10.00 per session
Children in receipt of Targeted Pupil Premium can attend Breakfast Club and the Early session free of charge, subject to places being available. There will be a charge for the late session.
Parents must complete a registration form before a booking can be made.
Parents are required to book their sessions via Arbor. Payment is taken at the time of booking. Click here for Arbor's guide on booking a Breakfast or After School Club via the Parent Portal or Parent App.
If you wish to use Tax Free Childcare Vouchers towards payment, the school needs to have an account with the voucher provider. We already have accounts with: the Government’s Tax Free Childcare scheme (Provider reference 118653), Edenred (Account Number: P21361608) and Bravo Benefits. If you have a different voucher provider, please send the details to the Kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk, so an account can be created.
Once the school has an account with your voucher provider, you can send payments via their website/portal. Please e-mail Kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk to confirm the amount sent. Once the payment is received into the school’s bank account (which can take a few days), Arbor will be credited with the voucher amount, allowing you to book your sessions.
If your child has additional needs, please contact the club before booking.
On the day bookings will be accepted if there are spaces.
For enquiries or changes, please contact:
kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk or call or text 07508841215
Parents need to email kingfisherclub@barham.kent.sch.uk if they wish to cancel a session, or your child is unable to attend. No charge will be made where at least 24 hours’ notice is provided. Sessions cancelled with less than 24 hours’ notice will still be charged, except at the school’s discretion.
Please collect children promptly at the end of their booked session. If you are running late, please contact the club immediately. There is a fee of £15 per child for a late collection, and you will be sent an invoice.
Guidance and Standards
The club operates in line with Department of Education wraparound childcare guidance and NSPCC safeguarding guidance.
By using Kingfisher Club, parents and carers agree to follow school policies and procedures and work in partnership with staff to support a positive and safe environment.

Attendance
Working Together to Support Excellent Attendance
At Barham Church of England Primary School, we want every child to attend regularly so that they can flourish academically, socially and emotionally. We know that attendance difficulties can occur for a variety of reasons and our approach is always to work in partnership with families, identifying and removing barriers wherever possible. Attendance concerns are managed through a graduated and supportive approach.
What Do Attendance Percentages Mean?
Approximate Days Missed in a School Year
Even small reductions in attendance can quickly add up. A child with 90% attendance misses the equivalent of almost four weeks of learning across a school year.
If your child is experiencing difficulties attending school, we encourage you to contact us as early as possible. Support may include:
If you are worried about your child's attendance for any reason, please contact:
